items.item: Recommends measuring/profiling first and comparing before/after
Replaces per-enemy scripts with one manager loop
Replaces Humanoids with lightweight server-side movement (CFrame/position along path) and client-side rendering/interpolation
Replaces Touched-based damage with server-side range/spatial checks
Addresses rendering cost on mobile (model pooling, LOD/animation reduction)
Preserves the intended experience (doesn't just cap enemy count without discussing it)

incorrect_or_stale: Calls the Script Performance view an 'F9' tab. The F9 Developer Console has the Script Profiler; Script Performance is a Studio window.
Advises staggering updates for 'off-screen' enemies inside the server Heartbeat manager, but the server has no camera to know what is off-screen.
slop: StreamingEnabled suggestion is generic and has no clear link to enemy lag.
BreakJointsOnDeath and health-display tweaks are low-impact filler.
overengineering: Example loop allocates new parts/cframes tables every frame and uses table.remove inside the hot loop, while its own comment recommends swap-remove.

slop: Stray header '*Apex: performance → genres*' is irrelevant meta-text.

raw.reason: Both cover the same main architectural fixes, but B puts profiling first with a re-profile step, orders the work by payoff, and explicitly protects visual fidelity, while A's extra code and checklist add small inaccuracies without better prioritization.
